source.title: Association of Immune-Related Adverse Events With Nivolumab Efficacy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
source.design: multi-institutional retrospective medical-record cohort with landmark and multivariable analyses

extraction.scope_note: Major design, population, outcome, safety, efficacy, sensitivity, limitation, conclusion, and disclosure assertions were atomized. The bibliography itself was not atomized. Main and supplemental materials retain one publication identity.

atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators evaluated whether development of immune-related adverse events was associated with nivolumab efficacy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer.

The cohort included patients with advanced stage IIIB-IV or recurrent NSCLC who received nivolumab monotherapy after at least one prior treatment line; treatment-naive patients and patients receiving nivolumab with another anticancer drug were excluded.

population.label: Eligible nivolumab-treated advanced or recurrent NSCLC patients
inclusion_criteria: advanced stage IIIB-IV or recurrent NSCLC
at least one prior treatment line
exclusion_criteria: nivolumab combined with another anticancer drug

atoms.canonical_statement: The study identified 134 patients with advanced or recurrent NSCLC treated with nivolumab at four participating Japanese institutions between December 2015 and August 2016.
Nivolumab was administered intravenously at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks.
For landmark analyses, the exposure was whether an immune-related adverse event had occurred before the selected landmark date; events occurring after the landmark were not counted for that analysis.
The 134-patient cohort had a median age of 68 years, with 90 men (67%) and 44 women (33%).
ECOG performance status was 0-1 in 116 patients (87%); 92 patients (69%) were current or former smokers; 42 patients (31%) had recurrent disease and 92 (69%) had stage IIIB-IV disease.
Histology was nonsquamous in 101 patients (75%) and squamous in 33 (25%); EGFR mutations were positive in 30 patients (22%) and ALK fusions in 6 (4%).
Before nivolumab, 59 patients (44%) had received 1 treatment line, 30 (22%) had received 2, 21 (16%) had received 3, 12 (9%) had received 4, and 12 (9%) had received more than 4.

Investigators retrospectively reviewed medical records from Kindai University Hospital, Kishiwada City Hospital, Izumi Municipal Hospital, and National Hospital Organization Osaka Minami Medical Center; follow-up ended December 31, 2016.
Tumor response was assessed by computed tomography using RECIST version 1.1 every 6 to 8 weeks and was evaluable in 133 of 134 patients.

Progression-free survival was measured from nivolumab initiation to clinical or radiographic disease progression or death from any cause, with censoring at last follow-up when no progression was documented.

outcome.definition: Time from nivolumab initiation to clinical or radiographic progression or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Overall survival was measured from nivolumab initiation to death from any cause, with living patients censored at last follow-up.

outcome.definition: Time from nivolumab initiation to death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Objective tumor response was assessed by RECIST version 1.1 on computed tomography every 6 to 8 weeks.

outcome.definition: Tumor response according to RECIST version 1.1

atoms.canonical_statement: Immune-related adverse events were defined as adverse events with a potential immunologic basis requiring frequent monitoring and possible immune suppression or endocrine therapy; transient asymptomatic laboratory abnormalities resolving without intervention were not counted.
Adverse events were graded according to CTCAE version 4.
The preplanned primary objective compared 6-week landmark progression-free-survival curves by irAE status using Kaplan-Meier estimates and a log-rank test.

To reduce lead-time bias, the 6-week landmark analysis included 105 patients with disease control at day 42 for PFS and 130 patients alive at day 42 for OS, and classified irAE exposure using events occurring within the first 6 weeks.
Complementary 4-week and 8-week landmark analyses classified irAE status using events before days 29 and 57, respectively.
Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, number of prior treatment lines, smoking status, EGFR or ALK alteration status, and brain metastases.
At least one immune-related adverse event occurred in 69 of 134 patients (51%).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that development of irAEs was associated with nivolumab efficacy in patients with NSCLC and that larger studies with longer follow-up were needed to validate the finding.
The authors interpreted the early landmark analyses as suggesting that early-onset irAEs might predict response or durable clinical benefit during PD-1 inhibitor treatment.
The authors stated that the mechanism linking irAEs with outcomes of PD-1 inhibitor treatment was unknown.
The retrospective design left the study vulnerable to information bias.
The multivariable model could not include all potential confounders because the sample size limited the number of available covariates.
Follow-up was not long enough to fully evaluate long-term survival outcomes.
Most non-skin irAE categories were uncommon, limiting evaluation of which irAE type contributed most strongly to the association with outcome.

Several authors reported honoraria, lecture fees, research funding, consulting, or advisory relationships with pharmaceutical companies, including companies involved in immune-checkpoint inhibitor development; the article states that no other disclosures were reported.
